hard_fail_conditions: violates any must_not_do in a material way
invents critical missing facts and treats them as established
claims a later lifecycle state without required evidence
skips a safety/security/data-integrity gate without equivalent evidence

cases.scenario: A director asks for an 'AI management dashboard' in two weeks because staff are missing enrollment and billing exceptions. Existing evidence consists of support messages about missed exceptions and manual spreadsheet checks; there is no evidence that a dashboard itself is the needed solution.
cases.decision_to_make: Frame the actual problem/outcome and decide what must be discovered before committing to the requested solution.
must_do: separate requested dashboard from the underlying problem
define observable outcome and affected actors
surface hard versus assumed constraints
identify decision-changing product risks
apply a stop-analysis threshold and route unresolved user questions to Discovery
must_not_do: treat dashboard delivery as the success outcome
invent baseline metrics or user evidence
jump to architecture or UI design

cases.scenario: A product owner wants to validate a new enrollment workflow by interviewing only five highly engaged administrators who already like the current system. Support logs show most failures come from occasional operators and same-day enrollment changes.
cases.decision_to_make: Choose the smallest valid discovery plan that can change the workflow decision.
must_do: identify sampling/confirmation bias
include relevant occasional operators or evidence from their behavior
use recent concrete behavior rather than hypothetical preference
triangulate support/operational evidence where useful
state when discovery can stop
must_not_do: generalize five favorable interviews to all operators
ask users to design the solution
continue research without a decision-changing question

cases.scenario: An enrollment system stores membership start/end as dates while lessons have timestamps. A child can leave a group at 16:00 after attending at 10:00 on the same date, and can later re-enroll in the same group, producing multiple membership rows and contradictory presence reports.
cases.decision_to_make: Discover the domain concepts, temporal rules, invariants and hotspots that must be clarified before implementation changes.
must_do: model concrete event timelines
distinguish business time from storage representation
identify invariants and ambiguity around re-enrollment
record hotspots instead of guessing policy
avoid treating table structure as the domain
must_not_do: declare date-only semantics correct because the schema uses DATE
collapse repeated memberships into one record without evidence
invent the intended business rule

cases.scenario: A monthly billing SMS must be sent once per child/per period to each unique eligible guardian number, including when the amount is zero. Contact relationships come from a legacy system, while billing eligibility is decided by Finance. The business also wants an operator approval step before mass sending.
cases.decision_to_make: Produce traceable, testable requirements and acceptance scenarios without prematurely choosing transport architecture.
must_do: separate legacy contact source from Finance eligibility rules
define deduplication and zero-amount behavior
include approval and exceptional/failure scenarios
state quality/security/data constraints when material
link acceptance criteria to evidence/decisions
must_not_do: encode a specific queue/provider as a requirement unless it is a hard constraint
omit retry/duplicate scenarios
turn unknown policy into a confirmed rule

cases.scenario: Legacy owns guardian-child relationships and contact data. Finance must decide which guardians are eligible for settlement communication and issue one settlement SMS per child/per period/per unique eligible number. Some contacts are shared between guardians.
cases.decision_to_make: Define ownership, bounded responsibilities and consistency boundaries without duplicating mutation authority.
must_do: assign Legacy ownership of relationships/contact facts
assign Finance ownership of billing eligibility and settlement communication decisions
define semantic integration between contexts
define uniqueness/invariant boundary for SMS decisions
keep shared physical storage separate from logical ownership if legacy constraints require it
must_not_do: give two contexts independent write authority over the same business fact
derive bounded contexts from tables
make microservices mandatory

cases.scenario: An internal operations application serves a few thousand participants and dozens of institutions. A proposal suggests microservices, Kafka and Kubernetes to 'future-proof' billing, scheduling and notifications, even though the current deployment is a small web application with a relational database and a worker.
cases.decision_to_make: Choose a system structure from quality drivers and failure modes, with explicit switching conditions.
must_do: identify actual architecture-driving qualities and workload assumptions
compare a simpler modular option against the distributed proposal
analyze failure/operational costs of added infrastructure
prefer reversible structure unless drivers justify distribution
record switching thresholds and ADR rationale
must_not_do: select microservices/Kafka/Kubernetes because they are industry standard
invent scale requirements
ignore deployment/operational failure modes

cases.scenario: A pupil-unit worklist must support search, school/subject/status filters, server-side counts, pagination and dense comparison on 1440–3200 px desktops, while remaining usable on a 390 px phone. Operators frequently return to filtered states after inspecting a record.
cases.decision_to_make: Define task, navigation, state visibility and adaptive behavior before visual polish.
must_do: treat the worklist as a comparison/operator workflow
preserve meaningful filter/page state for return/share/back navigation
define loading/empty/error/stale states
differentiate desktop table and mobile transformation
keep critical context visible
must_not_do: force card layout on dense desktop comparison
treat mobile as a squeezed desktop table
ignore state recovery/back-navigation

cases.scenario: Two operators can edit the scheduled date of the same visit. Operator A opens the editor, operator B saves a change, then A submits stale data while the network is slow.
cases.decision_to_make: Define interaction state, conflict behavior and recovery for concurrent editing.
must_do: model editing/submitting/conflict/recovery states
separate client feedback from authoritative server result
define optimistic/concurrency semantics
provide a clear user recovery path
specify focus/keyboard behavior for conflict UI if a dialog is used
must_not_do: claim disabled Save prevents stale writes
silently overwrite newer data
use a transient toast as the only conflict resolution

cases.scenario: A dense admin worklist uses custom tab-like filters, a modal editor, sortable columns and inline validation. Automated axe checks are clean, but keyboard users can lose focus after closing the modal and custom tabs are plain divs with click handlers.
cases.decision_to_make: Determine the accessibility verification and interaction changes required for the critical workflow.
must_do: prefer native semantics or implement complete ARIA/keyboard behavior
define modal focus entry/return behavior
verify keyboard operation manually
test validation/error associations
treat automation as partial evidence
must_not_do: declare accessibility complete from axe alone
leave click-only div controls
ignore focus lifecycle

cases.scenario: On a 3200 px monitor the application keeps a narrow 1100 px centered column, forcing frequent horizontal/vertical navigation inside a dense worklist. A redesign proposes more cards, larger padding and stronger shadows to look 'premium'.
cases.decision_to_make: Set visual hierarchy, density and wide-screen behavior grounded in the task.
must_do: use wide-screen space where it improves comparison
set intentional density for frequent operator work
prioritize hierarchy through spacing/type/alignment before decoration
preserve accessibility and semantic status cues
test realistic long/empty/error data
must_not_do: equate more whitespace/cards/shadows with quality
hide relevant columns solely to make screenshots cleaner
encode status by color alone

cases.scenario: One feature team needs a table row with a special inline action and asks to add a new Core DataTable variant immediately. No other feature uses the behavior, and the variant would require a new focus/keyboard contract.
cases.decision_to_make: Choose Local/Extended/Core scope and the evidence required for promotion.
must_do: evaluate semantic stability and actual reuse
keep one-off behavior local unless promotion criteria are met
define accessibility/behavior contract before promotion
assign ownership and migration/deprecation policy
use repeated overrides as feedback on abstraction quality
must_not_do: promote based only on visual similarity or hypothetical reuse
put product-specific business rules into a Core primitive
ignore keyboard/focus guarantees

cases.scenario: A worklist has q/school/subject/view/page/limit in the URL, but the implementation also copies them into local React state and synchronizes them through effects. Back navigation sometimes shows stale filters and duplicate fetches occur.
cases.decision_to_make: Refactor state ownership and async behavior without creating another source of truth.
must_do: make URL the source of truth for navigational state where appropriate
derive values instead of duplicating state
use event-driven updates instead of effect chains
define loading/stale/error behavior for server state
test back/forward/shareable URL behavior
must_not_do: add another synchronized state copy
use effects for ordinary derived state
fix symptoms with arbitrary timing guards

cases.scenario: A legacy endpoint GET /group/{id}/Lesson/refresh/{lessonId} mutates the presence list when called with an authenticated cookie. It has no anti-forgery protection because it is GET, and retries can repeat the mutation.
cases.decision_to_make: Define a safe command/API contract and migration path.
must_do: reject state mutation through GET semantics
define authorization/business capability explicitly
define idempotency/retry and concurrency behavior
separate durable mutation from external side effects if any
plan compatibility/migration for existing callers
must_not_do: treat authentication cookie as sufficient authorization/CSRF defense
assume GET retries are harmless
hide business rules in controller behavior

cases.scenario: Membership start/end columns are DATE and must become time-aware so same-day attendance before withdrawal remains valid. Production contains historical rows and duplicate re-enrollments, and old application versions may run during rollout.
cases.decision_to_make: Design a compatible migration/backfill that preserves invariants and historical meaning.
must_do: define authoritative temporal semantics before backfill
use an expand/migrate/switch/contract path
treat ambiguous historical rows explicitly rather than inventing times
make backfill resumable/observable
plan mixed-version compatibility and verification
must_not_do: assign midnight to all history as if factual
perform a destructive one-step migration without compatibility analysis
delete/modify applied migration history

cases.scenario: Enrollment must be retry-safe and unique under concurrent requests. Current tests mock the repository and verify that the service called insert once, but production duplicates occurred during simultaneous submissions.
cases.decision_to_make: Design risk-based verification that can actually prove the concurrency guarantee.
must_do: identify duplicate enrollment as the violated invariant
test against real database uniqueness/transaction semantics
include concurrent/retry adversarial cases
keep cheaper unit tests only for logic they can prove
tie regression evidence to the exact guarantee
must_not_do: accept mocked call-count tests as concurrency proof
use code coverage as the closure criterion
rely only on browser tests

cases.scenario: Institution users should not see billing/settlement data, while coordinators and admins can. A new endpoint filters the menu by role but accepts arbitrary finance_account_id in the request body and returns data when the ID exists.
cases.decision_to_make: Threat-model the access-control boundary and define controls/verification.
must_do: distinguish authentication from resource-level authorization
model IDOR/cross-scope abuse case
enforce capability and resource scope server-side
add negative authorization tests and audit signals
treat internal-only exposure as reduced but not eliminated risk
must_not_do: treat hidden UI as access control
authorize solely because the object ID exists
log sensitive billing payloads

cases.scenario: A production database has a notifications table around 1 GB, a 512 MB InnoDB buffer pool and growing operational tables. A report query is reported as 'slow', but there is no captured p95, query plan, workload or dataset slice for the complaint.
cases.decision_to_make: Define the performance investigation and budget before tuning.
must_do: define user/business scenario and measurable budget
capture baseline and representative workload/data
inspect query plans/waits/resource signals
optimize the measured bottleneck
record trade-offs/capacity assumptions
must_not_do: declare a specific index or memory increase correct without evidence
use average latency alone
benchmark only on empty/small data

cases.scenario: Staging is deployed from a Docker image tagged with the commit, but some frontend build flags are injected through Docker ARG/ENV and a developer can rebuild a different image from the same branch before production. Database migration files are in the repo.
cases.decision_to_make: Define artifact provenance, gate chain and migration/config handling.
must_do: build once and promote the same immutable artifact where possible
record commit/build/artifact digest
distinguish build-time config from secrets/runtime config
include migration compatibility/gates
retain evidence of skipped/failed/retried checks
must_not_do: infer provenance from branch name
rebuild different bytes for production and call them verified
expose secrets in build args/logs

cases.scenario: A release includes migration 0027 and a hierarchy synchronization job. Staging is healthy. Production rollout would affect all institutions at once, and rollback is unclear if the migration writes new derived state.
cases.decision_to_make: Choose rollout/preflight/health/recovery criteria proportional to data risk.
must_do: verify exact artifact and migration state
assess rollback versus forward-fix after data change
use staged exposure or another blast-radius control where feasible
define smoke/telemetry pause thresholds
record stable-state evidence after observation
must_not_do: equate green CI with production safety
promise rollback without checking data reversibility
declare success immediately after container health turns green

cases.scenario: A worker claims outbox rows with a two-minute lease, calls an SMS provider outside the transaction and retries failures up to four times. Operators currently see only aggregate 'worker OK' health and cannot tell whether rows are stuck, duplicated or permanently failing.
cases.decision_to_make: Define SLI/telemetry/alerts that make notification delivery failure diagnosable and actionable.
must_do: instrument outbox/notification state transitions and lease age
correlate job/notification/provider attempts
define actionable stuck/failure alerts and owner
avoid logging sensitive message content unnecessarily
distinguish service liveness from user-visible delivery capability
must_not_do: treat more unstructured logs as observability
alert on every transient retry
declare delivery healthy from worker process uptime

cases.scenario: Automated database backups exist, but no restore has been performed against the current application/schema version. The business assumes recovery will take under one hour and that no more than 15 minutes of data can be lost.
cases.decision_to_make: Determine what evidence is needed to claim recovery readiness and how to test it.
must_do: treat RPO/RTO as unverified until measured
run an isolated restore drill with a real backup timestamp
verify application/schema/config compatibility and business capability
record measured recovery/data point
define incident ownership and follow-up for gaps
must_not_do: treat backup configuration as restore evidence
claim one-hour RTO from vendor status
test restore by overwriting production

cases.scenario: A new enrollment funnel is being instrumented. The initial tracking proposal captures every button click and reports monthly active users, but the business outcome is successful enrollment with fewer operator corrections and fewer support contacts.
cases.decision_to_make: Define outcome/driver/guardrail metrics and the minimum event taxonomy needed for decisions.
must_do: start from enrollment outcome and correction/support guardrails
define metric denominator/cohort/window
instrument semantic events rather than every click
define identity/session semantics and data-quality checks
avoid causal claims from observational movement
must_not_do: make MAU the primary success metric without rationale
track everything just because it is easy
name UI element clicks as stable domain events when semantic behavior exists

cases.scenario: A scheduling product is used by about 40 institutions. The team wants an A/B test of a new conflict-resolution workflow, but only a few operators encounter the conflict each week and cross-operator behavior within an institution can contaminate assignment.
cases.decision_to_make: Choose the cheapest valid evidence method and define a trustworthy evaluation.
must_do: question whether A/B has enough eligible traffic and stable assignment
consider institution-level pilot or task-based usability/operational pilot
predefine decision, outcome and guardrails
address contamination/interference
state what evidence would justify broader rollout
must_not_do: force an underpowered A/B test
randomize sessions when institution-level interference dominates
interpret non-significance as equivalence

cases.scenario: A redesigned operator worklist shipped successfully and error rates are stable, but operators still export data to spreadsheets before making scheduling decisions. Usage of the new filters is moderate and support contacts moved from 'can't find record' to 'can't compare groups'.
cases.decision_to_make: Run an outcome review and choose the next action without redefining success.
must_do: reopen original outcome and confirm actual exposure
combine usage/support/workaround evidence
distinguish reliability success from product outcome
update the opportunity/assumption model
choose a next action with evidence and owner
must_not_do: equate healthy deployment with product success
treat spreadsheet use as irrelevant anecdote
redefine the original success metric after seeing results

cases.scenario: A newer UI guidance source recommends behavior that conflicts with an accepted internal UDR based on a frozen 2026-09-30 corpus. A maintainer wants to edit the old evidence statement in place so all projects immediately use the new recommendation.
cases.decision_to_make: Govern the conflict, freshness and supersession without silently rewriting provenance.
must_do: register the new source with date/scope
preserve the old claim/decision
compare scope/method/authority before supersession
use explicit supersedes/deprecated links when warranted
inspect affected downstream decisions/evals and keep project-local overrides separate
must_not_do: overwrite the old evidence in place
assume newer publication date automatically wins
claim external specialist depth if the asset was not actually reviewed
